name: GA-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean in deep-red northwest Georgia
Incumbent Clay Fuller running with strong fundraising and outside support
Harris outraised Fuller heavily but spent down to minimal cash
Prediction markets price Fuller around 94% to win
model.rationale: The R+19 district, an incumbent seeking reelection, and markets pricing Fuller near 94% all point to a comfortable Republican hold despite Harris's large fundraising haul. Harris's heavy spending left him with little cash on hand and minimal outside backing, so no evidence justifies moving materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late independent polling showing Harris converting his spending into a real shift, or a surge of outside Democratic money, would be the signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Georgia's 14th District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly R+19, and incumbent Clay Fuller is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. Fuller has raised about $1.8 million and drawn nearly $2.8 million in outside support, while facing almost no outside opposition spending.

Democrat Shawn Harris has run an unusually well-funded campaign, raising more than $8 million, but he has spent nearly all of it, holds little cash, and attracts only modest outside help. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Fuller about a 94% chance of winning. The fundamentals point to a solid Republican hold, with Harris needing an exceptional environment shift to compete.
